punchline: Tiger Woods met a golf club at age two, while Federer wandered through skiing, wrestling, swimming and football as a child.
thirty_sec: In David Epstein's Range, Tiger Woods stands for early specialisation and Roger Federer for branching out late. Federer played many sports as a child and locked onto one much later. According to Epstein, most elite athletes also tried several sports before finding their own. Early starters lead at first, but late samplers often catch up and pass them.
